**Rough volatility math (my calculation, not from a source)**
- Bitcoin's yearly volatility is about 40–55%. Over 10 days, that works out to a typical move (one standard deviation) of about 7–9%, or roughly ±$6,000–7,000.
- If prices follow that pattern, about 68% of outcomes would land between roughly $75,000 and $88,000, and about 95% between roughly $69,000 and $95,000.
- Over this short a window, the best simple guess for the median is today's price, around $81,500.

**Prediction markets**

**Resolution details**

criterios: This question resolves to the daily closing price of Bitcoin (BTC-USD) for October 30, 2026, in US dollars, as reported on the [Yahoo Finance BTC-USD historical data page](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BTC-USD/history/). The resolution value is the number shown in the "Close" column for the row dated Oct 30, 2026 (Yahoo's daily close is anchored to 00:00 UTC). For example, a close of $85,432.10 resolves as 85432.1.
letra_pequena: If the Yahoo Finance BTC-USD historical page is unavailable or does not report a value for October 30, 2026, the daily closing price for that date from [CoinGecko's Bitcoin historical data page](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin/historical_data) will be used instead. If neither source reports a value, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the BTC/USD closing price for October 30, 2026 will be used.
